KENNETH J. HOLLINSHEAD IN THE DELTA TAU DELTA GENERAL CATALOGUE, 1917
=====================================================================
Retrieved 2026-09-07 under p_430 (sweep the book corpus on the camp's PEOPLE, not on its name).
Source: "The Seventh General Catalogue of the Delta Tau Delta Fraternity" (1917), Internet Archive
item seventhgeneralca00delt, full djvu text downloaded whole (3,038,277 characters).

THE ENTRY, VERBATIM (line 7189):

    KENNETH  J.   HOLLINSHEAD,    Evanston,   111.      A.B.;    born  Port
    Clinton,  Ohio,  Sept.  5,  1886;  secretary,  Boys'  Y.M.C.A.

THE CHAPTER AND CLASS, from the catalogue's own index (line 68515):

    Hollinshead,  K.  J.,       Epsilon  '10

and the chapter roll is headed "EPSILON  ALBION" (lines 6451, 6552), so Epsilon is the ALBION
COLLEGE chapter and he is of the class of 1910. The class-year headings bracket him: '09 opens at
line 7152 and '10 at line 7179, with his entry at 7189.

WHAT IT GIVES THIS PROJECT
  BORN PORT CLINTON, OHIO, 5 SEPTEMBER 1886.
  A.B., ALBION COLLEGE, CLASS OF 1910.
  In 1917, at EVANSTON, ILLINOIS, occupation "secretary, Boys' Y.M.C.A."

HOW IT FITS THE MONTREAL RECORD, WHICH IS THE POINT
The YMCA of Montreal's 1910 annual report: "Next month Mr. K. J. HOLLINSHEAD, OF ALBION COLLEGE,
MICHIGAN, will take up the Boys' Secretaryship, which Mr. Murray Brooks resigned to go as
Strathcona Hall's representative in the Foreign Work in Ceylon." HE WAS THE CLASS OF 1910 AND
TOOK THE POST THE SAME YEAR -- straight out of college, at TWENTY-THREE. The 1913 report has him
leaving on 1 August 1913 "to take up Community Work", and this catalogue finds him four years
later still in boys' YMCA work, at Evanston.

A SECOND BOOK, NOT YET READ: "Faith made visible: the history of Floyd Starr and his school"
(1988), which mentions "... United States Senator, and KENNETH J. HOLLINSHEAD, NOW SECRETARY OF
THE ALBION COLLEGE ..." -- so he returned to his own college as its secretary. The snippet comes
from Open Library search-inside and the passage around it has NOT been read.

METHOD NOTE. Found by exact-phrase search on "Kenneth J. Hollinshead" at
openlibrary.org/search/inside.json -- three hits, all of them useful, where the same endpoint
returned 934, 346 and 190 hits of pure noise for M. G. Brooks earlier the same day. THE BOOK
CORPUS IS AN EXCELLENT INSTRUMENT FOR AN UNCOMMON NAME AND A USELESS ONE FOR A COMMON NAME, and
the difference is the whole skill in using it.
